simple.meaning: to bear young ; causatively, to beget ; medically, to act as midwife ; specifically, to show lineage
simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to יָלַד (H3205) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: v.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 500 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: יָלַד (yâlad) means to bear young ; causatively, to beget ; medically, to act as midwife ; specifically, to show lineage First listed occurrence: 1Chr 1 10.

definitions.short: to bear young ; causatively, to beget ; medically, to act as midwife ; specifically, to show lineage
definitions.usage: bear, beget, birth(-day), born, (make to) bring forth (children, young), bring up, calve, child, come, be delivered (of a child), time of delivery, gender, hatch, labour, (do the office of a) midwife, declare pedigrees, be the son of, (woman in, woman that) travail(-eth, -ing woman).

(Kö i. 404 f. ; perhaps יֹלֶדֶת intended by Kt, compare Sta § 213 b ); suffix Prov 23:25 ; יוֺלַדְתּוֺ 17:25 ; etc.; plural יֹלְדוֺת Jer 16:3 ; Passive participle יָלוּד 1Kin 3:26-27 , construct יְלוּד Job 14:1-2 t.; plural יְלוּדִים 1Chr 14:4 ; — 1 bear, bring froth: a. (a mother a child,) so commonly, approximately 208 t.; followed by accusative Gen 3:16 ; 4:1 & constantly; accusative omitted 6:2 etc. = be delivered of a child , 1Kin 3:17-18 , 2Kin 19:3 = Isa 37:3 (in proverb with negative, i.e. human power exhausted); of animals Gen 30:39 ; 31:8 (twice in verse); Jer 14:5 ; 17:11 (bird laying eggs, or hatching out young), Ezek 31:6 ; Job 39:1-2 , but also of whole process of labour (compare חול ) בְּלִדְתָּהּ וַתְּקַשׁ Gen 35:16 compare 35:17 , 38:27-28 , compare 1Sam 14:19 ; 30:6 ; 49:24 ; 50:43 ; Psa 48:7 , compare Hosea 13:13 ; עלבֿרכים ילד (Sta ZAW 1886, 143 ff. ) Gen 30:3 ; 50:23 (compare Job 3:12 ). c. figurative of wicked שָׁ֑קֶר וְיָלַד עָמָל וְהָרָה Psa 7:15 compare Job 15:35 also Isa 33:11 ; of Israelites, bringing froth wind (of vain efforts for deliverance) 26:18 ; יְלָדוֺ מִי שָׁמַיִם כְּפֹר Job 38:29 ; of Tyre as mother of her inhabitants Isa 23:4 of Jerusalem 51:18 ; 54:1 ; 66:7-8 , Ezek 16:20 ; Israel bearing disloyal children Hosea 5:7 ; Jerusalem and Samaria, as Oholibah and Oholah Ezek 23:37 ; of Babylon Jer 50:12 ; of a day, as producing events יוֺם יֵּ֫לֶד מַה לֹאתֵֿדַע Prov 27:1 ; perhaps of God (figurative of rock צוּר ), as mother of Israel bringing forth with labour Deut 32:18 yet see 2 less often beget: a. literal, approximately 22 t., always with accusative; in Hexateuch a mark of J; Gen 4:18 (3 t. in verse); 10:8 , 13 , 15 , 24 (twice in verse); 10:26 = 1Chr 1:10-11 , 13 , 18 (twice in verse); 1:20 , Gen 22:23 ; 25:3 ( Deut 32:18 & Num 11:12 E are dubious; P uses Hiph`il ), elsewhere Prov 17:21 ; 23:23-24 , Dan 11:6 . b. beget , figurative Psa 2:7 of ׳י s formally installing king into theocratic rights. 3 Zech 13:3 (twice in verse), of both parents (literally); Passive participle 3t. = child 1Kin 3:26-27 , where mother is named, 1Chr 14:4 where father named.
